simple.meaning: צָמַק (tsâmaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to dry up.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Hosea, beginning at Hosea 9:14. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.

simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: צָמַק (tsâmaq) / H6784 is traced through Hosea 9:14 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6784. tsamaq [ צָמַק ] vb dry up, shrivel (Late Hebrew id. ; ᵑ7 Num 6:3 צְמִיקִין , for יְבֵשִׁים ); — Qal Participle active plural צֹמְקִים שָׁדַיִם Hosea 9:14 shrivelling breasts (of women; || מַשְׁכִּיל רֶחֶם ).
